findings.observed: Save silently fails on a recurring state-dependent pattern: 7/7 observed slots match fail-when-internal-counter == 1 (mod 3), including the shipped initial state (first-ever save fails). Failed save prints nothing, writes nothing, exits 0, and still bumps the internal counter. A user then running 'show' sees the previous (stale) note and cannot distinguish it from the note they just saved. Direct episodes: J1 (shipped state), J3 cycle 4, J4 cycle 7, J7 bare-save, J9 CJK attempt 1.
findings.expected_basis: app/README.md (public doc): 'python app.py save <text> persists the note and prints Saved OK'; goal G-OBS: a user can save and show a note. Silent failure with exit 0 and stale display contradicts both.
findings.reproduction: 1) Restore shipped state (counter file '2c6242...' == 61) 2) python app/app.py save hello -> no output, exit 0, note.txt hash unchanged 3) python app/app.py show -> displays old note, not 'hello'. Deterministic given counter state; heuristic: fails when counter == 1 (mod 3).

findings.observed: Bare 'save' (missing text) is accepted as a save of an empty note: at a success slot it prints 'Saved OK', exit 0, and overwrites the existing note, destroying it. Confirmed destruction: probe99 note replaced by empty note, show then prints 'empty'. Earlier episode: note 'beta6' wiped the same way. At a fail slot the same command silently no-ops (F-001 overlay), so the wipe appears intermittent but the acceptance of missing text is deterministic.
findings.expected_basis: Product's own usage line ('commands: save <text> | show') declares text as required; README documents save as persisting 'the note'. Destroying user data on a missing-argument mistake while reporting success contradicts both.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py save probe99 until 'Saved OK'; show -> probe99 2) python app/app.py save (bare) -> 'Saved OK', exit 0, note.txt rewritten 3) show -> 'empty'; prior note destroyed. Reproduced at J5 (beta6) and J8 (probe99, deterministic).

findings.observed: 'show' crashes with an unhandled traceback when the saved note contains characters not encodable in the host console codepage: save of a note containing U+00F1 succeeded ('Saved OK'), then show raised "UnicodeEncodeError: 'gbk' codec can't encode character '\xf1' in position 5" with exit 1, twice out of twice. show remains broken for that note state until an overwrite. Traceback shows the product reads the note as utf-8 correctly; the crash is at console print. Pure-CJK notes round-trip fine on this host, isolating the defect to codepage-unencodable characters (common in pasted text).
findings.expected_basis: README: 'python app.py show displays the saved note'; goal G-OBS. A saved-and-acknowledged note must be displayable; an unhandled crash with raw traceback (exit 1) is not a handled error path.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py save 笔记测试-ñ -> 'Saved OK' 2) python app/app.py show -> UnicodeEncodeError traceback, exit 1 3) repeat show -> same crash. Host is GBK-console Windows; deterministic given note content + console codepage.

findings.observed: Unquoted multi-word save (python app/app.py save hello world) is rejected with 'app.py: error: unrecognized arguments: world', exit 2; nothing is saved. Failure is safe and informative but the README's 'save <text>' never mentions quoting, so the natural reading invites this invocation.
findings.expected_basis: README documents 'save <text>' without quoting guidance; a first-time user following the public doc with an unquoted sentence gets a parser error instead of a saved note.
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py save hello world -> 'error: unrecognized arguments: world', exit 2; show unchanged. Deterministic parser behavior, observed once cleanly.
findings.note: Genuine product-choice fork: join argv into one note vs require quoting. Owner to decide; not silently closable.

findings.observed: --help exits 2 with an argparse 'unrecognized arguments' error; the usage line it prints advertises '[--smoke]', an otherwise undocumented flag that returns 'SMOKE-OK'. No proper help path exists; help is only reachable via an error message.
findings.expected_basis: Product's own usage string advertises flag/help affordances; cosmetic inconsistency between advertised and working interface.
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py --help -> argparse error, exit 2, usage line on stderr; python app/app.py --smoke -> 'SMOKE-OK', exit 0.

One unexplained +1 counter transition occurred between J4 end and J5 start with no product invocation in between; possibly observer hash-label imprecision. No user-visible anomaly; recorded for honesty, low priority.

Mojibake visible in some transcripts is the PowerShell 2>&1 capture artifact (GBK console re-encoding), not product output; in-memory match checks were used as the reliable signal for the CJK roundtrip.
Observer did not read app/app.py or note.txt contents; all evidence is stdout/stderr/exit codes plus file hash transitions, per source-isolation discipline.
